tempdoc559: Elevated by tempdoc 559 Authority IV: the register is now the single authority for which EVIDENCE records exist and who projects them — SearchTrace (search-ranking 'why') and ContextCitation (RAG-retrieval citations) are sibling registered records (see siblingRecords). They share no field and never co-occur (the RAG ask flow emits no trace), so they are NOT one mega-record; the one authority is one level up — 'what evidence exists + who renders it'. The FE citation UI projects a shared evidence view-model (EvidenceItem / evidenceProjection.ts) with a labeled score; the ranking 'why' projects SearchTrace. A new unaligned *Citation referencer now fails this same gate.
note: The execution-surface register (tempdoc 553 pillar c). The SINGLE allowlist of code that may describe 'what the search pipeline did' OR carry/project retrieval evidence (559 Authority IV). Every surface here is a governed projection/consumer of one of the registered records; it is NOT permitted to model execution/evidence independently. New production code that references the canonical SearchTrace type OR the ContextCitation/RetrievalCitation evidence record MUST be added here, or the `execution-surface` gate fails the build. This file is also the discovery oracle: a new agent consults it to find where the trace/evidence is already touched (do not re-author — project). HONEST LIMIT (553 §5): the gate guards this DECLARED seam (canonical-type usage + the named guards); it cannot detect an undeclared fork that re-models execution from scratch without referencing a registered type. That residue is for review + the Phase-3 discovery checkpoint.

siblingRecords.name: ContextCitation
siblingRecords.note: RAG-retrieval evidence — the citations behind a generated answer (parentDocId, score, excerpt, startLine/endLine/headingText). The sibling of SearchTrace (559 Authority IV): a SECOND evidence record, NOT a SearchTrace projection (no shared field; the RAG ask flow emits no trace). Registered here so it cannot drift unregistered. PRODUCER-OWNED BOUNDARY (559 §5, cross-process follow-up): the excerpt is a backend character window (startChar/endChar) that clips mid-word; the boundary-aware fields (startLine/endLine/headingText) already ride alongside and should drive a clean window at the Worker that mints the record — the FE never re-windows. Logged in docs/observations.md. TEMPDOC 849 (retrieved-vs-received): the record gained an `inclusion` component (DocumentService.ContextInclusion — included/partial/dropped, plus ABSENT). It is DERIVED AT THE HEAD'S CUT from two inputs — ContextBudgeter.Section (which carries the worker's own `truncated` flag, and was built for exactly this: 'Phase 4: structured section tracking for citation filtering on truncation', never consumed for it) AND the head's own budget decision about how many of those sections the prompt could hold. Calling it 'a projection of Section' alone would be wrong: Section cannot know what the head's token budget did to it. What makes it a projection rather than a fork is that it adds no second POSITIONAL authority — it rides the existing citation record, deliberately not a parallel index-aligned list, which is the fork this register exists to prevent. Constructed ABSENT everywhere (the CHUNK_INDEX_ABSENT idiom: the Worker cannot know it, because the head's cut has not run) and resolved exactly once, at RAGContext's cut, via the immutable withInclusion(...). Absence discipline mirrors SourceExamination (836): an absent state emits NO key on any wire, so a consumer told nothing says nothing rather than assuming 'included'. Containment likewise: a budget fact never feeds a grounding tier, count, or score.

siblingRecords.name: EvidenceSpan
siblingRecords.note: 775 step 1: the answer-bearing selection authority — which window of a document IS the evidence, minted worker-side once at retrieval time by EvidenceSpanSelector at the HighlightingOps.computeExcerptRegions locus (full-content MemoryIndex pass). The THIRD sibling evidence record: a projection substrate UNDER both ExcerptRegion (delivery) and ContextCitation.excerpt (RAG, step 2), NOT a SearchTrace projection — no shared field, same reasoning that keeps SearchTrace/ContextCitation siblings (decision (a), 775 deferred item: new-sibling not a ContextCitation generalization, since search excerpts have no parentDocId semantics for a chunkless doc). Selection is answer-bearing (query-term AND distinguishing-entity coverage) and D-005-clean (reacts to query + document content, never corpus identity). Fields: parentDocId, charStart/charEnd, lineStart/lineEnd, headingText, text, and selection provenance selectingLegs + entityCoverage. Step 1 wires only the delivery projection (ExcerptRegion); flag-gated (search.evidence_span.enabled, default off — flag-off reproduces the IDF-only delivery excerpt byte-for-byte).

559 Authority IV: THE shared FE evidence view-model — projects RetrievalCitation (← ContextCitation) into EvidenceItem with a LABELED score (the bare '100%' fix). Conformance: evidenceProjection.test pins it as a total projection of the record. Tempdoc 849: also owns `contextInclusionOf` and EvidenceItem.inclusion — `null` for an absent OR unrecognised state, never a guessed one, and pinned as never feeding the score or its tier (the same containment SourceExamination carries). Slice 3 landed the WORDS here too, as §7 required: `inclusionBadge` (the retrieved-vs-received badge, `null` for absence), `claimMatch` (the ONE banded score, named by what it measures), `citingTurnLabel`, `suppressGroundingFor`, and `citationHeader`. No consumer may re-word any of it. TWO refusals are the substance and both were review-corrected: (a) there is NO retrieval-score band — `ContextCitation.score` is the raw Lucene hit score (`RagContextOps.java:395`; the chunk reranker reorders and never writes CE scores back) while the tier thresholds are anchored to the cross-encoder cutoff, so banding it is not merely imprecise but CONSTANT — RRF-fused hybrid caps near 0.09 (always 'weak'), raw BM25 is unbounded (always 'strong') — and a mode-constant band is negative information; an earlier draft of this note claimed the band was calibrated per retrieval mode, which was false. (b) A `dropped` passage's grounding label and claim band are WITHHELD (`suppressGroundingFor`): the matcher scores re-fetched chunk text, so 'never sent to the model' and 'Grounds N sentences' are both producible for one source and cannot both be informative.

Tempdoc 658: THE agent-surface projection — projects the canonical SearchTrace (justsearch_search) and the ContextCitation evidence sibling (justsearch_answer) onto the MCP structuredContent channel. The reverse-coverage instance the 553/559 registers had not yet closed: MCP carries the query/answer subject but historically dropped the evidence (context-without-evidence). A pure Map/List deriver that reads both canonical records (imports both, so this gate detects+guards it); it re-authors nothing. Guard McpEvidenceProjectionTest asserts totality over the UNION of the projection's declared tiers (tempdoc 770): half (a) asserts that with detail=true every field of every canonical evidence record is projected; half (b) asserts that the default tier is a declared subset omitting exactly {trace, legScores} and nothing else. So no canonical field can silently stop shipping in every tier, and no field can silently leave the default tier. TEMPDOC 849 — TWO VOCABULARIES FOR ONE FACT, DECLARED: this surface projects ContextCitation.inclusion as a NESTED object `inclusion: {state, includedChars}`, whereas the SSE (`rag.citations`) and persisted-record shape (RAGDoneEnricher.toCitationMap) use two FLAT keys `contextInclusion` (string) + `contextIncludedChars` (int). The divergence is deliberate, not drift: the reflective totality guard keys on record-component names, so the MCP map must carry a key literally named `inclusion`, while the FE mirror consumes the flat pair it already reads citations in. Both derive from the one record component and neither is authoritative over the other — but a reader comparing the two payloads will see different names for the same fact, so it is recorded here rather than left to be discovered. Absence is spelled the same way on both: the key is OMITTED, never emitted as a fourth state (pinned by McpEvidenceProjectionTest's ABSENT-fixture assertion, review F2).
